overview.title: What is Gelephu Mindfulness City?
overview.text: Gelephu Mindfulness City is a Special Administrative Region in Bhutan, blending Buddhist heritage with modern economic development across 2,600 km².

overview.title: Who joins Gelephu Mindfulness City?
overview.text:
Remote workers, entrepreneurs, and digital professionals can join through the [Digital Nomad Residence Programme](https://partners.digitalgmc.com), launched in early 2026 in partnership with NomadClub. The programme grants a 12-month renewable Bhutan residence permit with no minimum income requirement and no mandatory minimum stay.

Business founders and investors in GMC's eight priority industries - spanning fintech, green energy, spirituality, wellness, education, and aviation - can incorporate companies and obtain financial services licenses under GMC's Singapore-modeled legal framework. A fast-track licensing pathway exists for firms already regulated in Singapore, Abu Dhabi Global Market, or Hong Kong.

history.text:
Gelephu Mindfulness City began with a royal vision. On 17 December 2023, His Majesty King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck [announced the project](https://gmc.bt/speech) during the 116th National Day celebration to 30,000 attendees, calling it "a Mindfulness City, encompassing conscious and sustainable businesses, inspired by Buddhist spiritual heritage, and distinguished by the uniqueness of the Bhutanese identity." Alongside the announcement, [BIG (Bjarke Ingels Group)](https://www.archdaily.com/1011445/big-unveils-gelephus-mindfulness-city-bridging-bhutans-heritage-and-future) with Arup and Cistri unveiled a masterplan featuring eleven mandala-inspired neighborhoods and three bridge-axes housing key civic infrastructure.

Royal Charter No. 1 of 2024, granted on 13 February 2024, formally established GMC as a Special Administrative Region with its own executive, legislature, and judiciary - independent of the Royal Government of Bhutan. The Application of Laws Act took effect on 26 December 2024, adopting 18 Singaporean laws and 10 Abu Dhabi Global Market financial regulations as the governing legal framework.

Construction of the Gelephu International Airport began in 2025. In November 2025, Lee Seow Hiang (former founding CEO of Changi Airport Group) and Pang Yee Ean (former Director General of Investments at the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank) were appointed as Co-Chief Executive Officers. By early 2026, the city launched the Digital Nomad Residence Programme. On 21 February 2026, His Majesty announced [Project 108](https://gmc.bt/108) - the initiative to raise 108 Jangchub Chortens simultaneously on 1 November 2026.

location:
Gelephu Mindfulness City occupies Bhutan's southern plains in Sarpang District, on the border with India's Assam state and roughly 250 km south of Thimphu. The Special Administrative Region spans over 2,600 km² - approximately three times the area of Singapore - transitioning from subtropical lowland plains in the south to Himalayan foothills in the north.

The masterplan by [BIG (Bjarke Ingels Group)](https://www.archdaily.com/1011445/big-unveils-gelephus-mindfulness-city-bridging-bhutans-heritage-and-future) with Arup and Cistri preserves 96% of the land as productive landscape, paddy fields along rivers, and wildlife corridors that maintain undisturbed migration routes for elephants and other wildlife. Built development covers just 4% of the total area, with buildings limited to 3-6 stories and constructed using local wood, stone, and bamboo.

Eleven mandala-inspired neighborhoods connect via three major bridge-axes, each anchoring key civic infrastructure: an international airport, a university and knowledge campus, and a healthcare center for Eastern and Western medicine. The international airport is currently under construction and will serve as the city's primary aviation and logistics gateway. The [Project 108](https://gmc.bt/108) sacred landscape will extend 12 km along the Mau Chhu river when all 108 Jangchub Chortens are completed in November 2026.
duration:
The [Digital Nomad Residence Programme](https://partners.digitalgmc.com) issues 12-month renewable residence permits with no mandatory minimum stay. A permit may be renewed once, allowing a maximum continuous stay of 24 months under current programme terms.

Business entities and licensed financial services firms operate on timelines set by their individual licensing agreements with the Gelephu Financial Services Office. GMC is a permanent city under phased construction through 2035 - there are no cohort cycles or fixed programme end dates for residents and investors.
pricing:
The [Digital Nomad Residence Programme](https://partners.digitalgmc.com) costs $2,800 per year in programme fees paid to the Gelephu Mindfulness City Authority, plus a $10,000 deposit held in TER tokens at DK Bank of Bhutan. The TER deposit is fully refundable upon exit. There is no minimum income requirement and no mandatory minimum stay period.

For businesses, GMC offers 0% corporate tax for priority-sector companies (fintech, green energy, and other designated industries), 0% capital gains tax, no withholding tax on dividend distributions, and income tax relief for foreign employees through 2030. Standard corporate tax is 17% under GMC's Singapore-modeled one-tier system, with losses carrying forward indefinitely.
amenities: 12-month Bhutan residence permit, renewable to 24 months
Freedom to reside and travel throughout all of Bhutan (not restricted to Gelephu)
Sustainable Development Fee waived (saves $100 per day versus standard tourist entry)
DK Bank digital banking account with multi-currency access across nine currencies
0% tax on foreign-sourced income (only Bhutan-sourced earnings are taxed)
Access to curated global nomad community via NomadClub partnership
Natural setting of Himalayan foothills, subtropical forests, and the Mau Chhu river corridor
BTC-backed lending and digital asset services through DK Bank
Fast-track business licensing pathway for firms already regulated in Singapore, ADGM, or Hong Kong

howToEnter.text:
Applications for the Digital Nomad Residence Programme are processed through [Digital Bhutan by NomadClub](https://partners.digitalgmc.com). The four-step process typically completes in 48-72 hours: verify eligibility (must be a remote professional, entrepreneur, or self-employed individual in a field aligned with GMC's priorities), submit your application and pay the $2,800 programme fee to the GMCA, open a DK Bank account with a $10,000 TER deposit, then receive your 12-month Bhutan residence permit.

For business licensing and investment, contact the Gelephu Mindfulness City Authority at [gmc.bt](https://gmc.bt/). Companies already licensed in Singapore, ADGM, or Hong Kong qualify for an expedited licensing review. For [Project 108](https://gmc.bt/108) patronage (starting at $200,000 per chorten) or to register as a volunteer for the 1 November 2026 raising day, contact [108@gmc.bt](mailto:108@gmc.bt).

faqs.question: What is Gelephu Mindfulness City and how does it differ from a typical SEZ?
faqs.answer: Gelephu Mindfulness City (GMC) is a Special Administrative Region in southern Bhutan with its own laws, executive authority, and judiciary - separate from the Royal Government of Bhutan. Unlike a typical special economic zone focused primarily on tax incentives, GMC is built around Bhutan's Gross National Happiness philosophy: low-rise eco-friendly architecture, 96% of land preserved as nature, eleven mandala-inspired neighborhoods, and industries spanning spirituality, wellness, green energy, and fintech alongside aviation and logistics. The city is in active construction, with the international airport, the Project 108 sacred landscape, and first-phase infrastructure currently underway.

faqs.question: Where exactly is Gelephu Mindfulness City located?
faqs.answer: GMC is in Sarpang District, southern Bhutan, on the border with India's Assam state and approximately 250 km south of Thimphu. The region covers over 2,600 km² of subtropical lowlands that transition into Himalayan foothills. A new international airport is under construction to serve as the primary travel gateway.

faqs.question: How can I live and work in Gelephu Mindfulness City?
faqs.answer: The primary entry route is the Digital Nomad Residence Programme, operated in partnership with NomadClub. It grants a 12-month renewable Bhutan residence permit with no minimum income requirement and no mandatory stay. [Apply at partners.digitalgmc.com](https://partners.digitalgmc.com). Initial approval typically takes 48-72 hours.

faqs.question: How much does the Gelephu Mindfulness City Digital Nomad Residence Programme cost?
faqs.answer: The programme fee is $2,800 per year, paid to the Gelephu Mindfulness City Authority. Applicants also deposit $10,000 in TER tokens at DK Bank - this deposit is fully refundable when you exit the programme. There is no minimum income requirement and no mandatory minimum stay period.

faqs.question: What is the TER token and why is a deposit required?
faqs.answer: TER is a gold-backed digital token issued by GMC on the Solana blockchain, launched in December 2025. The $10,000 TER deposit at DK Bank serves as a financial commitment and is fully refundable upon exit. Holding TER also gives access to DK Bank's digital asset services, including BTC-backed lending and multi-currency accounts across nine currencies.

faqs.question: What is Project 108?
faqs.answer: Project 108 is an initiative to build 108 Jangchub Chortens (Buddhist monuments), each 15 meters tall, along the Mau Chhu river in Gelephu, spaced 108 meters apart over roughly 12 km. All structures are to be raised simultaneously on 1 November 2026, following His Majesty's announcement on 21 February 2026. Individual chorten patronage starts at $200,000 USD. At least 40,000 volunteers are needed for the raising day - no specialist skills required. To volunteer or inquire about patronage, contact [108@gmc.bt](mailto:108@gmc.bt) or visit [gmc.bt/108](https://gmc.bt/108).

faqs.question: What are the tax benefits for businesses setting up in Gelephu Mindfulness City?
faqs.answer: Priority-sector companies pay 0% corporate tax. All businesses benefit from 0% capital gains tax, no withholding tax on dividend distributions, and an indefinite loss carry-forward provision. Foreign employees receive income tax relief through 2030. Standard corporate tax is 17% for other business types under GMC's Singapore-modeled one-tier system.

faqs.question: Who leads Gelephu Mindfulness City?
faqs.answer: His Majesty King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck chairs the Board of Directors. Co-Chief Executive Officers are Lee Seow Hiang (former founding CEO of Changi Airport Group) and Pang Yee Ean (former Director General of Investments at the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank and founder of Urbina Capital). Board members include Joichi "Joi" Ito (President of Chiba Institute of Technology and former Director of MIT Media Lab), Arun Kapur (founder of Druk Gyalpo's Institute in Paro), and Lauren Chung (Asia Pacific CEO of Teneo).

faqs.question: When will Gelephu Mindfulness City be fully built?
faqs.answer: The masterplan phases development through 2035. Phase one targets roughly 100,000 residents; the long-term vision is a city of one million people. As of 2026, the international airport is under construction, Project 108 is underway, and the Digital Nomad programme is active. Planned civic facilities - the university, hospital, cultural center, and hydroelectric dam-temple - have not yet been built.

faqs.question: Is Gelephu Mindfulness City part of Bhutan?
faqs.answer: Yes. GMC is a Special Administrative Region within the Kingdom of Bhutan under a "One Country, Two Systems" framework. It has its own legal system (modeled on Singapore and ADGM law), an independent judiciary, and separate executive authority, but remains under the constitutional monarchy of His Majesty the King.

faqs.question: Can crypto and fintech companies set up in Gelephu Mindfulness City?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Gelephu Financial Services Office issues Financial Services Licenses for virtual asset trading, institutional custody, and other regulated activities. In May 2026, GMC launched a fast-track licensing pathway for firms already regulated in Singapore, Abu Dhabi Global Market, or Hong Kong. BTSE Bhutan was the first exchange to receive in-principle approval. Multi-currency banking including digital asset services is available through DK Bank.

faqs.question: Do I need to stay in Gelephu, or can I travel throughout Bhutan with the residence permit?
faqs.answer: The residence permit grants freedom to reside and travel throughout all of Bhutan - it is not restricted to Gelephu. Standard tourists must pay Bhutan's Sustainable Development Fee of $100 per day when traveling; residence permit holders have this fee waived, making extended Bhutan travel significantly more accessible.
